school_p: Every public school student in California gets free breakfast and lunch. No form needed.
sun_p: {m} per child each summer, on a card. Kids on {snap} or Medi-Cal get it automatically.

pantry_p: Most pantries need no ID and don't ask about immigration status. Some ask your income or ZIP.
mm_p: Market Match adds extra money for fruits and vegetables when you spend {snap} at the market, often up to {m} a visit. Ask at the info booth.
imm_p: Since April 2026, many refugees, asylees and parolees can no longer get {snap}. Children who are citizens can still get it. Food banks, WIC and school meals are open to families of any status.
work_p: Since June 2026, adults 18 to 64 without kids under 14 may need to work, train or volunteer 80 hours a month to keep {snap}. Many people are excused, like pregnant people and people who can't work.
scam_p: Applying is always free. Never share your PIN, and change it if anything looks wrong. If benefits are stolen, call the number on the back of your card right away.
senior_hint: Shows senior food boxes in the main list.
your_data_p: Your area, saved recipes, list and prices are stored only on this device. Erasing removes all of it.
pv_lead: Plenty Map is built so we know nothing about you.
pv_1: Nothing that identifies you. There are no accounts, ads, cookies, trackers or analytics.
pv_2: Your ZIP code or location is used on your device to sort places by distance. It is never sent anywhere. The app only downloads the lists for your general area (about 50 km across) from our site.
pv_3: The quick check for benefits runs on your device and is never saved or sent.
pv_4: Your area, saved recipes, list and prices are stored on your device. You can erase them any time in Settings.
pv_h2: Where the app gets its data
pv_5: All lists and recipes come from our own site, plentymap.com, and map pieces from our own map server, tiles.plentymap.com, run by Cloudflare. The app talks to no one else.
pv_6: Like any website, our web host may keep short-lived technical logs, such as IP addresses, for security. We don't use them to track anyone.
pv_7: If you tap Directions, Call or a website, your device opens that app or site, and their own privacy rules apply.
pv_8: Plenty Map is safe for all ages. It collects nothing from anyone, including children.
pv_9: We will never sell, share or rent anything, because we have nothing to sell.

us_find_p: Stores and farmers markets that take {snap}, plus food pantries, free meals and community fridges.
us_note_meal: Few free meal sites are listed online. Dial 2-1-1 to hear about the ones near you.
us_note_market: Every market here takes EBT. Markets marked “Extra for produce” add money for fruits and vegetables when you pay with {snap}. Markets run on set days, so check before you go.
us_listings_note: Listings may be incomplete in your area. Plenty Map is still growing, and we're adding local food sources as fast as we can. Until then, your local food bank and 2-1-1 can point you to every pantry nearby.
us_data_note: Stores and listings checked {d}. Plenty Map is not run by any food bank or government office.
us_urgent_p: In most of the U.S., a real person answers day or night, in your language, and can tell you where to get food today. The call is free.
us_results_note: This is a guess, not a decision. Only your state's office decides, and applying is free.
us_cf_alt: Your income is over {g} a month, but some homes can qualify up to {g2}, like homes with child care costs or someone 60+ or disabled. Apply and let the office check.
us_assets: Savings count too: up to {a}, or {b} if someone is 60+ or disabled. Your home doesn't count.
us_ak_note: These are the amounts for Anchorage and other cities. Rural Alaska gets more.
us_wic_p: Healthy food, formula help and baby support. Income limit is {g} a month for your home, and anyone on Medicaid or {snap} qualifies.
us_school_p: Kids in homes that get {snap} get free school meals with no form. Other families can apply at school, and many schools serve free meals to every student.
us_sun_p: Many states give {m} per child for groceries each summer. Kids on {snap} or Medicaid often get it automatically. Ask your state if it takes part.
us_ais_p: Hot lunches at senior centers, and meals brought to your home if it's hard to get out. For people 60 and older. The Eldercare Locator connects you to your local office.
us_rmp_p: If you get {snap} and are 60+, disabled, or without a home, you can buy hot meals with your EBT card at restaurants near you that take part.
us_mm_h: Get more for fruits and vegetables
us_mm_p: Many farmers markets and some stores add extra money for fruits and vegetables when you pay with {snap}. Look for “Extra for produce” on the Find food tab.
us_imm_p: Under new federal rules, many refugees, asylees and parolees can no longer get {snap}. Children who are citizens can still get it. Food banks, WIC and school meals are open to families of any status.
us_work_p: Under new federal rules, adults 18 to 64 without kids under 14 may need to work, train or volunteer 80 hours a month to keep {snap}. Many people are excused, like pregnant people and people who can't work.
us_pr_p: Puerto Rico has its own program instead of SNAP, run by ADSEF. You can apply at an ADSEF office or online.

note_summer: Free meals for anyone 18 and under during summer break. No forms, no ID. Sites open and close through the summer, so check the dates.
note_garden: Many gardens rent plots for a small fee or free, and some share extra produce. Ask before you pick.
note_givebox: Small free boxes run by neighbors. Take what you need, leave what you can. What's inside changes.
note_bakery: Bakery outlet stores sell day-old bread and snacks for much less. Many take EBT; ask at the register.
rep_note_h: Please don't include your name, phone number or other personal details.
rep_sends: Sends only this listing, the problem you picked and your note. No location, no name, no device details.

rep_failed: That didn't send. Check your connection and try again, or
rep_flag_closed: People reported this place closed recently. Call before you go.
rep_flag_hours: People reported the times or address may be wrong. Call before you go.
summer_p: During summer break, kids and teens 18 and under eat free at schools, parks and libraries. No forms. Text "summer meals" and your ZIP code to {tx} to find sites.
us_school_all: Every public school student in {st} gets free breakfast and lunch. No form needed.
us_sun_no: {st} did not take part in SUN Bucks ({m} per child) in summer 2026. Free summer meals for kids still run in every state.
sfmnp_p: Many states give people 60 and older with low income checks or a card for fresh produce at farmers markets each summer. Sign up early in spring; spots fill up.
mow_p: Meals brought to your door for people 60 and older, and in many places for adults with a disability. Many programs also serve meals at senior centers. Cost is free or by donation for most.
life_p: If you get {snap}, Medicaid or SSI, Lifeline takes up to {m} a month off your phone or internet bill ({b} on Tribal lands). One per home.
online_h: Discounts when you shop online with EBT
online_p: Amazon Prime Access is {a} a month. Walmart+ Assist is {w} a year. Instacart drops the delivery or pickup fee on EBT orders at many stores. All three need you to show you get {snap} or Medicaid.
online_note: EBT pays for food only. Delivery fees, tips and taxes need another card.
surplus_p: Too Good To Go sells bags of a store's or bakery's unsold food for about a third of the price. Flashfood sells groceries near their date at a big discount at partner stores.
surplus_note: Flashfood takes EBT at Meijer, Tops, Giant Eagle, Lucky and Piggly Wiggly. These apps are run by other companies.
freeprod_p: Community gardens and little free pantries are run by neighbors. Bread outlet stores sell day-old bread for less. Food banks often run gleaning days where volunteers pick extra produce from farms; ask yours.
kd_p: Restaurants where kids eat free or for a dollar or two, usually with an adult meal. Pick a day.
kd_disclaimer: Deals change often and many restaurants run them only at some locations. We list what was published and when we last checked. Call the restaurant before you go.
